visuals.title: The autoimmune company it keeps
visuals.text: Female sex is the biggest risk factor; look for other autoimmune disease in her or her family.

visuals.title: Where the symptoms come from
visuals.text: Liver inflammation gives jaundice, RUQ pain and hepatomegaly; joints give arthralgia.

glossary.Hepatocytes: The main working cells of the liver.
glossary.Hepatocellular: Relating to the liver cells themselves rather than the bile ducts.
glossary.Transaminases: Liver enzymes ALT and AST, released into the blood when liver cells are damaged.
glossary.Anorexia: Loss of appetite (here a symptom, not the eating disorder).
glossary.Malaise: A general feeling of being unwell or lacking energy.
glossary.Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes from raised bilirubin in the blood.
glossary.Bilirubin: Yellow breakdown product of haemoglobin, cleared by the liver into bile.
glossary.RUQ: Right upper quadrant of the abdomen, where the liver and gallbladder sit.
glossary.LFTs: Liver function tests: blood levels of ALT, AST, ALP, GGT, bilirubin and albumin.
glossary.Graves' disease: Autoimmune overactive thyroid caused by antibodies that stimulate the TSH receptor.
glossary.Type 1 diabetes: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells, leaving the body unable to make insulin.
glossary.Autoimmune thyroid disease: Thyroid disorders caused by autoantibodies, such as Hashimoto's thyroiditis or Graves' disease.
glossary.Premenstrual: Before periods have started, meaning girls before puberty in this context.
glossary.Autoantibody: An antibody that wrongly targets the body's own tissue.
glossary.Liver biopsy: Taking a small core of liver tissue with a needle to look at under the microscope.
glossary.Gold standard: The most accurate test available, against which others are judged.
glossary.Serology: Blood tests for antibodies or antigens, used here to detect viral hepatitis.
glossary.Viral hepatitis: Liver inflammation caused by hepatitis viruses A to E.
glossary.Immunosuppression: Treatment that dampens the immune system to stop it attacking the body.
glossary.Immunology: Blood tests of the immune system, such as immunoglobulin levels and autoantibodies.
glossary.Maintenance: Long-term lower-dose treatment to keep the disease in remission.
glossary.Liver transplant: Surgical replacement of a failing liver with a donor liver.
glossary.Autoreactive T-cells: T lymphocytes that recognise and attack the body's own antigens.
glossary.Antigens: Molecules that the immune system recognises and responds to.
glossary.Collagen: Tough structural protein laid down as scar tissue in fibrosis.
glossary.B-cell: Lymphocyte that matures into plasma cells which make antibodies.
glossary.Pathophysiology: How a disease disrupts normal body function to cause its features.
glossary.Organ-specific: Autoimmune disease aimed at one organ, such as the thyroid or pancreas.
glossary.Ultrasound: Imaging using sound waves, used to look at liver texture and exclude other causes.
glossary.Remission: A period where the disease is controlled and blood tests normalise.
